beats.head: Bruncraft Lands $1.1B Fleet Order as Vane Pivots From Cuts to Growth
beats.body: Bruncraft Industries secured a $1.1 billion multi-year contract to supply 14,000 Coachline and Vanguard-trim vehicles to national courier operator Melloway Freight, its largest fleet deal in five years. CEO Marcus Vane framed the win as validation of the leaner Coachline relaunch, noting deliveries begin in the third quarter and run through 2029. Vane hinted at further fleet negotiations, saying the cost reset has 'freed the company to chase volume again.'

beats.head: Bruncrest Works Unveils Aria Ultra X, Doubling Throughput Per Line
beats.body: Bruncrest Works revealed the Aria Ultra X, a redesigned compute unit that CEO Ines Marlow said delivers roughly twice the throughput of the current generation while cutting power draw by a third. Marlow claimed the breakthrough lets a single production line match the output of two, easing the margin pressure that dogged last quarter's third-line push. Early commitments from three data-center customers already exceed $3 billion, the company said.

beats.head: Brunmark Motors Returns to Beat as Veyra Relaunch Finds Traction
beats.body: Brunmark Motors posted quarterly revenue of $6.3 billion, ahead of guidance, as redesigned Veyra deliveries climbed 22% sequentially and warranty claims on the new battery pack fell sharply. CEO Iris Calvagh said the turnaround had 'turned the corner,' with the halted Veyra S line set to resume limited production early next year. Margins recovered to 8.1% as the prior quarter's relaunch costs rolled off.

beats.head: Dunmorewright Edges Past Estimates as Waterworks Crosses Halfway Mark
beats.body: Dunmorewright Industries reported the $780M waterworks contract has passed its halfway milestone two weeks ahead of schedule, lifting quarterly billings 6%. CEO Emil Skarn credited the expanded foundry capacity for holding delivery timelines steady through a tight materials market. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance.

beats.head: Fennvale Mfg. Beats Again as Fasteners Volume Joins Auto-Parts Strength
beats.body: Fennvale Mfg. topped estimates for a third straight quarter as its ramped auto-parts line held full volume and fasteners orders rose 9%. CEO Theo Vossen said the plant's steady output had earned Fennvale two new supply agreements with regional assemblers. The company nudged its full-year revenue outlook higher.

beats.head: Garrware Breaks Ground on Sixth Marrow Valley Line as Demand Holds
beats.body: Garrware began construction on a sixth production line at its Marrow Valley complex following three straight quarters of tight backlog. CEO Orla Holt said the $95 million addition should come online within a year and lift packaging throughput by an estimated 12%. Holt characterized the move as 'measured, in step with committed orders.'

beats.head: Holtforge Group Wins $640M Interconnector Contract, Extending Backlog Into 2030
beats.body: Holtforge Group secured a $640 million wire-and-cable supply contract for the cross-regional Saltmere interconnector, its largest single award to date. CEO Yvette Bramm said the deal locks in production through 2030 and builds on the record order book behind the company's recent beat streak. Work is expected to begin ramping late this year.

beats.head: Ironcrestton Opens Flagship Ateliers in Four Cities as Aurelian Demand Runs Hot
beats.body: Ironcrestton will open four new flagship ateliers over the next 18 months, backed by a $210 million investment, after the Aurelian Collection outpaced supply. CEO Corwin Vale said the expansion targets waitlists that have stretched past six months on signature pieces. The move marks the house's first retail footprint growth since Vale retired the Meridian line.

beats.head: Boreas Power Energizes First Compute-Paired Campus Under $4.5B Supply Pact
beats.body: Boreas brought its lead compute-paired campus online, the first delivery against the $4.5B anchor supply agreement. Mira Thorne said two further sites will follow within twelve months, lifting committed capacity across the program to 1.9 gigawatts. The house reaffirmed its widened $3.2B build plan remains fully financed.

beats.head: Fennmoor Beats as New Medical Diagnostics Division Posts First Combined Profit
beats.body: Fennmoor topped estimates as the unified Halquist-Carrow diagnostics division delivered its first profitable quarter since the mergers. Dorian Brandt said cross-selling into existing Devices and Industrial Machines channels drove diagnostics revenue up 22%, with integration savings tracking ahead of plan. Brandt hinted the house is 'far from done' scouting further medical targets.

beats.head: Halhold Works Ousts CEO Anselm Rocha as Board Moves On From Aveline Recall Fallout
beats.body: Halhold's board removed Anselm Rocha after the Aveline Successor recall swelled to an estimated $410M in charges and gutted Devices margins. Chair Idris Vale said the company needs 'stability and a clean safety culture' after two quarters of turbulence. Veteran operations chief Naomi Fenwick steps in immediately, pledging a full audit of the Wire & Cable and Medical Equipment lines.

beats.head: Korrworks Beats as Third-Hub Anchor Tenant Begins Ramp-Up Payments
beats.body: Korrworks topped forecasts as early lease and fit-out payments from its third-hub anchor tenant flowed through the books ahead of schedule. Rhys Throne said the $260M material-handling contract is now roughly 40% installed, with the hub tracking toward a phased opening. Management nudged full-year guidance higher on the faster ramp.

beats.head: Varnvale & Sons Unveils Corvane Perpetual Line Built on In-House Thessaly Cases
beats.body: Varnvale launched its Corvane Perpetual collection, the first line fully cased at the recently acquired Thessaly Works. Bram Wold said vertical integration cut per-unit case costs by 18% while enabling a limited run priced above the house's prior flagships. Early allocations to Fine Goods boutiques are already committed through the season.

beats.head: Vossenspire Supply Strikes $620M Deal for Coachbuilder Meridian Carrosserie, Deepening Vehicles Push
beats.body: Fresh off three straight beats, Quinn Marrow unveiled the acquisition of storied coachbuilder Meridian Carrosserie for $620M, the house's largest outlay in a decade. Marrow said the deal hands Vossenspire bespoke bodywork capacity to pair with its Timepiece momentum, targeting a combined luxury order book north of $2B. Integration will run through a new Vehicles Atelier arm led by longtime lieutenant Sabine Corriveaux.

beats.head: Aperture Compute Rocked as Emberline Safety Records Found Altered
beats.body: An internal review disclosed that inspection logs at the Emberline fabrication site were falsified ahead of the earlier regulatory probe, prompting the suspension of two site executives. CEO Marisol Venn called the findings 'unacceptable' and pledged a full external audit, but regulators signaled the probe will now widen to document tampering. Shares came under heavy pressure as several customers requested contract reviews.

beats.head: Castlehold Ousts Voss as Board Installs New Chief After Framework Collapse
beats.body: Castlehold's board removed CEO Halden Voss following the collapse of the Framework deal, the $600M charge, and the second-plant shutdown, naming turnaround veteran Ingrid Mally as chief executive. Mally said her first priority is resolving the outstanding regulatory probe and stabilizing grid-storage operations before pursuing new mandates. The board also suspended forward guidance pending a strategic review.

beats.head: Halcrow & Vance Wins $4.2B Coastal Reclamation Program in Largest Award to Date
beats.body: Halcrow & Vance secured a multi-year $4.2B earthmoving mandate for the Corveth coastal reclamation program, the largest single award in the company's history. CEO Mira Skarn said the deal, layered atop the ongoing Vetask work, will require a fourth yard and roughly 900 additional operators. Management flagged phased revenue recognition beginning next quarter.

beats.head: Greywater Grid Ousts Renwick as Board Installs Crisis Chief Amid Discharge Fallout
beats.body: Greywater Grid's board removed CEO Sable Renwick as the discharge scandal and $2.4 billion partner lawsuit engulfed the company, naming restructuring specialist Halden Voss to stabilize operations. Voss inherits a regulatory probe, a fractured compute partnership, and mounting demands for a full audit of the closed-loop reservoir claims. Directors said the leadership change was necessary to 'restore credibility with regulators and counterparties.'

beats.head: Marlgear Supply to Exit Consumer Devices, Slash 3,200 Jobs in Blakely Overhaul
beats.body: Marlgear Supply announced a sweeping restructuring that will wind down its consumer device unit and cut roughly 3,200 jobs as CEO Corin Blakely retreats to its industrial machines core amid the Kessel fault fallout. The company will take a $900 million charge and set aside reserves against the pending $1.4 billion suit and criminal referral. Blakely called the move 'painful but the only path to a clean, defensible business.'

beats.head: Woldmark Lands $2.1B Meridian Supply Pact as Sonn Bets Big on Capacity
beats.body: Woldmark secured a landmark $2.1 billion multiyear supply agreement to furnish Meridian compute units to a consortium of enterprise buyers, its largest single contract since the Halcyon era. CEO Petra Sonn, characteristically bullish, pledged to double Meridian output within eighteen months and called the deal 'proof the comeback is real.' The pact locks in volume commitments that analysts say could underpin revenue guidance for years.

beats.head: Vossenspire Holdings Hit With $1.6B Investor Suit Over Storage-Bank Probe Disclosures
beats.body: A consolidated shareholder action alleges Vossenspire concealed defects in its storage-bank line for nearly two years before the probe forced Halden Roe's ouster. The complaint seeks $1.6B and names former leadership, though it also drags newly split units into discovery. Maren Vok said the company would 'defend vigorously' while warning the litigation could overshadow the post-probe overhaul for several quarters.

beats.head: Brunstone & Sons Ousts Frost as Board Seeks Steadier Hand After Vault II Whiplash
beats.body: The board removed Dagny Frost following the demand shortfall and 1,400-job restructure that erased her earlier recovery claims, naming operations chief Ansel Voight as chief executive effective immediately. Voight pledged a 'no-surprises' operating plan and paused all further Vault II capacity decisions pending a demand review. Shares had swung violently through Frost's tenure of bold public reversals.

beats.head: Erretmark Works Faces Cross-Border Probe Into Veyron Braking Systems After Fleet Reports
beats.body: Regulators in two of Erretmark's continental markets opened a joint investigation into braking-component failures on roughly 40,000 Veyron units delivered under the $2.1B fleet accord. Aurelia Garr said the company is 'fully cooperating' and has paused new Veyron deliveries pending review, a move that could disrupt the record delivery cadence touted last quarter. The fleet customer has withheld part of a scheduled payment.

beats.head: Calderworks Lands $780M Corridor Framework as Fifth Kiln Draws Sweeping Structural Orders
beats.body: Calderworks signed a $780M multi-year framework to supply structural materials across the expanding Vaultridge corridor, its largest single agreement on record. CEO Kestrel Halloran said the fifth kiln would be dedicated almost entirely to the pact, with output committed through 2031. The deal locks in demand well beyond current record kiln capacity.

beats.head: Castlestone Unveils Grid-Core Ascend Platform as Karsh Bets Comeback on New Compute Line
beats.body: CEO Pell Karsh took the stage to launch Grid-Core Ascend, a next-generation compute platform he called "the reason we survived the reset," pledging shipments within two quarters. The company committed $1.9B to production tooling and named the landmark contract signed last quarter as the anchor customer. Karsh, characteristically bold, told the room the platform would double throughput per unit or he would "answer for it personally."
